title: Stipple wave

reference.source: Reference 12: teal stipple print, 614 × 1228 px PNG (rows of brush dabs in S-curves).
reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: Rows of brush dabs along an S-wave, rendered only as dot density: dense rounded tips, fading tails, a haze between, every dot the same 2 px.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 614 × 1228 and every length scales with the canvas

wave.does: How far the rows swing from side to side.

wavelength.does: Length of one full S across the sheet.

rows.does: Distance between rows of dabs; tails of one row reach into the next.

group.does: Inked rows in each sweep before the gap.

gap.does: Rows left almost empty after each sweep, which is the white between sweeps.

cross.does: A second system of rows running the other way, laid under the first.

pitch.does: Spacing of dabs along a row.

width.does: Radius of each dab's solid lobe; the tail behind it is as wide.

length.does: How far the tail runs before it ends.

flare.does: How much the tail widens along its length; at 1 it ends twice as wide as the tip.

floor.does: Tone the tail never falls below, as a share of the lobe; it is what fills the band between lobes.

fade.does: Distance over which the density falls to a third of the tip.

tip.does: Dots per pixel at the tip; above 1 the dots pile up into a solid.

haze.does: The thin even field of dots between the rows.

cell.does: Pitch of the grid the tone is dithered on; dots cannot sit closer than this.

dot.does: Side of every square dot; the reference's cover a 2 × 2 px footprint.

grain.does: Per-cell scatter of the tone before it picks an ink; 0 makes each tone a clean mix, 2 throws dark dots into the haze.

seed.does: Re-rolls the dab jitter and the ink choice per dot.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: A dab tip: dots pile up to nearly solid; the rounded edge is a density edge, not a drawn one.

techniques.name: Tone
techniques.implementation: The tail: the same dots, fewer of them, with the light ink mixed in as the dark thins out.

techniques.name: Pull
techniques.implementation: Rows stacked: one row's tails reach the next row's tips, so the sheet reads as scales.

techniques.name: Flow
techniques.implementation: The S-bend: dabs fan slightly on the outside of the curve because they are spaced by arc length.

techniques.name: Paper
techniques.implementation: Flat paper: no fiber, no tint; the only texture on the sheet is the dot.

techniques.name: Edge
techniques.implementation: Row ends at the sheet edge: the density field runs off the paper without a border.

pass_order: flow: a tilted sine wave; rows are its level sets, with arc length along each row tabulated so dab spacing holds around the bends
dabs: on each row, a dab every pitch with a rounded tip of the dab's radius and a tail that fades exponentially and ends; every fourth row is thin, so rows read as sweeps
a second, mirrored sweep system laid under the first
haze: a thin even field between the rows, slightly clumped
stipple: each pixel draws a dot with probability 1 - exp(-density); the dot lands at a hashed sub-pixel offset
ink: dark or light by a chance that rises toward the tips; dots multiply into the paper, so overlaps go darker

measured.dot_footprint: 2 × 2 px bounding box for 39 of 51 area-4 dots in a sparse field; component area median 4

row_spacing_px.method: 2-D autocorrelation peak of the smoothed darkness at r = 47.8 (top band) and 52 (lower band)

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Teal stipple palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: The sweep is generated, so the out rects for the dense tips, the tail field and the band edge were placed with search.py; the sparse field and the whole plate compare in place.

limits: Under 98 %: the tone histograms of every patch (0.79 to 0.84) and the lag-1 autocorrelation of the dense patches. The reference was dithered at a finer cell and scaled up by a non-integer factor, which spreads every 2 px dot over partial pixels and flattens its histogram; the square-dot splat at a 2 px cell keeps the dot but not that flattening.
The transfer table was read per pixel with a nearest-ink rule, so partial-coverage pixels of mid dots were counted as pale; the sparse field therefore carries more pale dots than the reference.
The sweep is an original arrangement; the reference's rows are not traced.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
